program.pageDescription: The Forever Sixty creator program: $2 for each player who comes back, half of their Premium for a year, paid monthly through Stripe.
program.lead: If you stream or make videos about World of Warcraft: Forever, you can earn from the players you send us.

sections.title: What you get
paragraphs: $2 for each player you send who comes back. A player comes back when they sign in with Battle.net, import at least one Forever character, and use the site again on a later day within 14 days of signing up.
Half of the Premium they pay, after Stripe’s fees and any refunds, for 12 months from their first payment. Guild plans count when the officer who pays came through you.
Both add up: $2 once when a player comes back, then half of each of their payments for a year.
Premium on your own account and the Raid guild plan for your guild while you are in the program.

sections.title: How players count
paragraphs: You get a link of your own and a code. Your code gets viewers a free month of Premium, or a free month for their guild; they enter it when they subscribe, and a card is still needed. A player is yours if their first visit came through your link within 30 days before they signed up, or if they use your code.
Each account counts once, for one creator. Accounts made before you joined, and your own account, never count.

sections.title: Payouts
paragraphs: Each month closes on the 1st. We approve it during the first week and pay it through Stripe to a payout account you set up with them. We never see your bank details. A month under $10 carries over to the next one. Each creator has a monthly cap, $500 unless we agree another.

You can see your players by week, and what you have earned, on your own stats page. A player counts as coming back up to 14 days after signing up, so the latest weeks fill in late. We never show you who they are.
Stripe asks for your tax details when you set up payouts. If you leave the program, your free Premium ends, and the months you already earned are still paid.

sections.title: Saying it is sponsored
paragraphs: You earn money when people use your link or code, so you have to say so wherever you share it. Say “affiliate link” or “sponsored” on stream or in the video, and put the same words next to your link or code. The FTC and Twitch both require it, and so do these terms: the first time it is missing we warn you, and a second time ends your place in the program.
